title: Etale-proetale comparison for supported sections and their exterior products
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finite commutative ring. All coefficient categories below are ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf of rings $A$, not condensed coefficient categories. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], separated in the diagonal sense [def-weil-proper-morphism], a closed subscheme $C\subseteq T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $M\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with its bounded-below inverse image as in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
c^C_{T,M}:R\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{et}},M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_T^*M),
$$
natural in $M$ and compatible with open restriction and forgetting supports. Here both support functors are the ordinary right-derived sections with support [def-pur-support-cohomology]. For $C=T$ this map is the global-sections comparison induced by the comparison adjunction unit.

Let $Z\subseteq X$ and $W\subseteq Y$ be closed subschemes of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and suppose $F=K\boxtimes_A^L L$ is bounded below. Products are fibre products over $k$ [def-pc-base-change], with projections $p_X,p_Y$, and $K\boxtimes_A^L L$ means $p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$. Put $K_p=\nu_X^*K$, $L_p=\nu_Y^*L$, $P=X\times_kY$. Let
$$
\theta:\nu_P^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}K_p\boxtimes_A^L L_p
$$
be the composite of the canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the comparison pullback identifications [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The supported exterior products [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] in the two topologies satisfy the equality in $D(A)$, the unbounded derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$
R\Gamma_{Z\times_kW}(P_{\mathrm{proet}},\theta)\circ c^{Z\times_kW}_{P,F}\circ\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}
=\kappa^{Z,W}_{K_p,L_p}\circ(c^Z_{X,K}\otimes_A^Lc^W_{Y,L}).
$$
The pro-etale exterior product here is defined by pulling back and tensoring supported sections, derived with K-flat tensor and injective support resolutions in that topology. The assertion concerns comparison of these maps; it does not assert a Kunneth isomorphism in either topology.

proof.text:
Write $H^\tau_{T,C}=R\Gamma_C(T_\tau,-)$, computed on unbounded complexes by K-injectives and agreeing with [def-pur-support-cohomology] on bounded-below objects. By [lem-pur-derived-support-comparison-direct-image] there is a natural isomorphism
$$b_{C,N}:H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}(R\nu_{T,*}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}(N),$$
normalized by the support-kernel equality. For $M\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ set
$$c^C_{T,M}=b_{C,\nu_T^*M}\circ H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}(\eta_M).$$
The unit is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], so $c^C_{T,M}$ is an isomorphism. Naturality follows from those of $b$ and $\eta$. The forgetting-supports and open-restriction squares follow by applying the corresponding restriction maps to the same kernel equality and using the canonical inverse-image restriction comparison; the two squares commute by the elementary functoriality of kernels. For $C=T$, the support kernel is global sections, and the normalization is precisely [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology].

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify etale and pro-etale support objects and transport restriction, forgetting supports, and the full-support normalization.

proof.text:
We use auxiliary sheaves only within the proof. For either topology, with $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$, set
$$Q^\tau_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!A_{T\setminus C}\to A_T).$$
The arrow is induced by the inclusion of the open object into the final object. The free-module Yoneda bijection [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], followed by sheafification, identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,N)$ with $N(T)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A_{T\setminus C},N)$ with $N(T\setminus C)$. Here the free sheaf on the open object is $j_!A_{T\setminus C}$ by the explicit definitions [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Therefore the cokernel universal property gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q^\tau_{T,C},N)=\ker(N(T)\to N(T\setminus C)).$$
For any open object $V$ of $T$, adjunction and the direct-image formula give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\nu_T^*(j_{V!}A_V),N)=\operatorname{Hom}(j_{V!}A_V,\nu_{T,*}N)=N(V)=\operatorname{Hom}(j_{V!}A_V,N),$$
where the first free sheaf is etale and the last is pro-etale. The resulting canonical isomorphisms for $V=T$ and $V=T\setminus C$ intertwine the arrows induced by inclusion, since both arrows represent restriction. The exactness of $\nu_T^*$ then gives a specified isomorphism $\nu_T^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\cong Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$, preserving these quotient generators.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support), with the free-sheaf Yoneda description of sections and the cokernel universal property; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EJ (remark-localize-presheaves).

proof.text:
For the quotient sheaves of step 2, [lem-pur-support-quotient-flat] gives flatness in both topologies and K-flatness in degree zero. The fixed-$A$ tensor and tensor over the constant ring sheaf agree after sheafification directly from [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], since constant scalars are locally elements of $A$. Put $P=X\times_kY$ and $S=Z\times_kW$. The generator multiplication of [lem-pur-support-quotient-product] gives
$$e_\tau:p_X^*Q^\tau_{X,Z}\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*Q^\tau_{Y,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^\tau_{P,S}.$$
Its ordinary sheaf map sends $\overline a\otimes\overline b$ to $\overline{ab}$. The comparison normalization is the elementary consequence of the generator-preserving comparison in [lem-pur-support-quotient-flat], naturality of pullback in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and the derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus no separate comparison lemma is needed, and the pro-etale assertion uses comparison pullback rather than geometric-stalk conservativity.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: verify tensor, pullback and quotient-generator multiplication on the two support objects.

proof.text:
For a complex $V$ of $A$-modules let $\underline V_T^\tau$ be its termwise constant sheaf and put
$$E^\tau_{T,C}(V)=Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A^L\underline V_T^\tau.$$
This is the termwise exact functor $V\mapsto Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A\underline V_T^\tau$: constant presheaves are exact and module sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], and the quotient sheaf is flat by step 3. Tensor and sheafification universal properties, together with step 2, give the ordinary adjunction
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A\underline V_T^\tau,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,\Gamma_C(T_\tau,N)).$$
A map $\sigma$ on the left corresponds to $v\mapsto\sigma(\overline1\otimes v)$; this section is supported on $C$ because the quotient generator restricts to zero on $T\setminus C$. The exact functor on the left is its own derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. The right adjoint has a right derived functor on all complexes: compute it on the K-injective resolutions of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The derived adjunction of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] is therefore
$$E^\tau_{T,C}:D(A)\rightleftarrows D(T_\tau,A):H^\tau_{T,C}.$$
Alternatively, on complexes the displayed Hom adjunction shows that $\Gamma_C(T_\tau,J)$ is K-injective when $J$ is K-injective, by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]; the bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] then gives this adjunction directly. Denote its counit by $\varepsilon^\tau_{T,C,M}:E^\tau_{T,C}H^\tau_{T,C}M\to M$. This construction concerns the ordinary support-kernel functor, not a choice of a closed pro-etale exceptional inverse image.

proof.text:
Step 2 and the tensor comparison give a canonical identification $E^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}=
u_T^*E^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$. Here $
u_T^*\underline V_T^{\mathrm{et}}=\underline V_T^{\mathrm{proet}}$: it holds for the free rank-one module by step 2, and hence for a presentation of any $A$-module by coproducts of free rank-one modules, since inverse image and sheafification preserve colimits. Apply this termwise and use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The unbounded adjunction $
u_T^*\dashv R
u_{T,*}$ follows by the exact-derived adjunction argument of step 4, using [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]; only its unit on bounded-below objects is claimed to be an isomorphism. The composite of $E^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\dashv H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ with $
u_T^*\dashv R
u_{T,*}$ has right adjoint $H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}R
u_{T,*}$, identified with $H^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ by the actual kernel equality $b$ in step 1. Its Hom bijection is the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Under it, the transpose of $
u_T^*\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C,M}$ is exactly $b\circ H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}(\eta_M)=c^C_{T,M}$. Consequently the counits satisfy the explicit identity
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C,
u_T^*M}\circ E^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}(c^C_{T,M})=
u_T^*(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C,M}).	ag{*}$$
The equality uses the identification of the two $E$ functors just specified. It holds for every bounded-below $M$ and is an equality of derived morphisms, not merely of the maps on their cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with the composite adjunction counit calculation; proetale.tex Tag 09B1 (lemma-compare-derived).

proof.text:
For $P=X\times_kY$ and $F=K\boxtimes_A^L L$, the canonical tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] followed by the comparison pullback identifications [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives the stated isomorphism $\theta:\nu_P^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}K_p\boxtimes_A^L L_p$. The bounded-below hypothesis on $F$, and exactness of $\nu_P^*$ from [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], allow step 1 for this coefficient complex and ensure that the pro-etale target is bounded below. For either topology, step 3 and the tensor comparison also give, for arbitrary $V_1,V_2\in D(A)$,
$$d_\tau:E^\tau_{P,S}(V_1\otimes_A^LV_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}p_X^*E^\tau_{X,Z}(V_1)\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*E^\tau_{Y,W}(V_2).$$
Use $e_\tau^{-1}$ on the quotient sheaves and the canonical tensor and constant-sheaf pullback identifications, preserving the order of the factors. These $d_\tau$ commute with comparison: $e_{\mathrm{proet}}$ was the pullback of $e_{\mathrm{et}}$ in step 3, and all remaining maps are the canonical pullback-tensor maps normalized on total tensor complexes in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The composition and identity comparisons of inverse images are monoidal by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]; their $A$-module comparisons follow by imposing the scalar balancing relations in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus no additional scalar or sign is inserted in this square.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), normalized by its K-flat total-complex proof; proetale.tex Tag 09B1 (lemma-compare-derived).

proof.text:
Write $B_\tau=H^\tau_{X,Z}K_\tau$ and $D_\tau=H^\tau_{Y,W}L_\tau$, with the coefficients in the statement. By [lem-pur-supported-product-quotient-model], the quotient adjunctions of step 4 identify with the normalized $C_a$ adjunctions of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] and [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product], preserving their counits. Under these identifications the map $d_\tau$ of step 6 is the tensor comparison in those definitions: for ordinary modules, precompose both maps with the epimorphism $e_h$ (etale) or $q_h$ (pro-etale). On $1\otimes(v_1\otimes v_2)$ each composite is the tensor of the two pulled-back quotient maps, since $e_\tau^{-1}(\overline 1)=\overline 1\otimes\overline 1$. The defining uniqueness of the quotient factorization therefore gives equality. Apply this equality on every bidegree summand of the signed direct-sum total complexes, without exchanging factors. On K-flat representatives it gives equality of the localized comparisons; [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] then gives equality of the natural derived maps. Thus the specified products are the transposes of
$$m_\tau=(p_X^*\varepsilon^\tau_{X,Z,K_\tau}\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*\varepsilon^\tau_{Y,W,L_\tau})\circ d_\tau:E^\tau_{P,S}(B_\tau\otimes_A^LD_\tau)\longrightarrow K_\tau\boxtimes_A^LL_\tau.$$
This equality holds before forgetting supports and does not require $B_\tau\otimes_A^LD_\tau$ to be bounded below.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the tensor and counits with the specified supported exterior-product maps.

proof.text:
Compare the two requested morphisms by their transposes under $E^{\mathrm{proet}}_{P,S}\dashv H^{\mathrm{proet}}_{P,S}$, using the identification with the $C_h$ adjunction and normalized $\vartheta_{\mathrm{proet}}$ from [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] established in step 7. By naturality of its counit, identity $(*)$ for $(P,S,F)$, and the definition of $m_{\mathrm{et}}$ in step 7, the transpose of the left-hand side is
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}\circ E^{\mathrm{proet}}(H^{\mathrm{proet}}(\theta)\circ c^S_{P,F}\circ\kappa_{K,L})=\theta\circ\nu_P^*m_{\mathrm{et}}.$$
For the right-hand side, naturality of $d_{\mathrm{proet}}$ moves $E^{\mathrm{proet}}(c^Z_{X,K}\otimes_A^Lc^W_{Y,L})$ through $d_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its transpose is consequently
$$\bigl(p_X^*(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}_{X,Z,K_p}\circ E^{\mathrm{proet}}_{X,Z}(c^Z_{X,K}))\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}_{Y,W,L_p}\circ E^{\mathrm{proet}}_{Y,W}(c^W_{Y,L}))\bigr)\circ d_{\mathrm{proet}}=\theta\circ\nu_P^*m_{\mathrm{et}},$$
using $(*)$ for the two factors and the explicit comparison compatibility of $d$ from step 6. The adjunction bijection therefore gives the displayed equality of the item. The source $B_{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_A^LD_{\mathrm{et}}$ need not be bounded below; step 4 deliberately constructed its adjunction on $D(A)$, while the three coefficient complexes to which $(*)$ is applied are bounded below by the hypotheses and step 6.
